name: Minecraft PE
description: The Original Minecraft Pocket Edition App! Enlisted on the Android Market on October 7, 2011. Later releasing on iOS on November 17, 2011
controversy_description: From 2011, Minecraft PE has had several controversies before its Bedrock transfer which are: Extreme Lack of Features, The Pocket Limitations, Performance Issues, Replacement of Free Content and Hardcore Limitations/Slow Updates compared to Java Edition and Bedrock Edition.

name: Minecraft PE Lite
description: A free, limited version of Minecraft Pocket Edition designed to showcase the game before purchase. Featured a small world, limited blocks, and no survival mode.
controversy_description: Criticized for being extremely restricted, lacking survival mode, and not receiving updates after early 2012. Many users viewed it as abandoned even before the full PE matured.

name: Google+
description: Google’s attempt at a social network, integrating Circles, Hangouts, and Google services. Initially launched as an invite-only platform before expanding globally.
controversy_description: Faced criticism for forced integration with YouTube comments, low user engagement, and a major data exposure incident in 2018 that accelerated its shutdown.

name: Google Talk
description: Google’s original instant messaging service using the XMPP protocol. Supported text chat, VoIP, and integration with Gmail before being replaced by Hangouts.
controversy_description: Criticized for inconsistent feature support across platforms, gradual abandonment in favor of Hangouts, and the eventual shutdown of XMPP federation which alienated long-time users.

name: Android Market
description: The original app distribution platform for Android devices before its rebranding to Google Play in 2012.
controversy_description: Known for weak security, rampant malware, and inconsistent app quality control. The rebrand to Google Play was partly an attempt to distance from these issues.

name: Google Listen
description: A podcast discovery and listening app created by Google Labs, offering early podcast subscription syncing with Google Reader.
controversy_description: Abandoned after Google Reader’s shutdown, leaving users without migration tools. Seen as another example of Google killing niche but beloved services.

name: Google Shopper
description: A barcode and image-based shopping comparison tool that let users scan products to find prices and reviews.
controversy_description: Criticized for inaccurate price listings and slow scanning performance. Eventually merged into Google Search and discontinued.

name: Google Goggles
description: An early visual search app allowing users to identify objects, landmarks, and text using the phone camera.
controversy_description: Praised for innovation but criticized for inconsistent recognition accuracy. Later replaced by Google Lens.

name: YouTube Remote
description: An app that allowed Android phones to act as remote controls for YouTube Leanback on TVs and computers.
controversy_description: Users complained about connection instability and lack of updates. Eventually replaced by native casting features.

name: Google Currents (Classic)
description: A magazine-style news and article reader that aggregated content from publishers and RSS feeds.
controversy_description: Replaced by Google Play Newsstand, then Google News, making it one of Google’s many short-lived content apps.
